answer: Tidal inlet quota: each epoch admits at most S=ceil(N/9) new identities, allocated by sealed auction for one non-transferable copper anchor. A farm must bid for every alias each epoch; capacity stays scarce while the anchor price floats up with demand. Each anchor binds to one hardware attestation and dies with it, so renting compute cannot mint keys. The river of admission is public: winning bids and anchor bindings replay from the ledger, and duplicate hardware across two anchors voids both. Honest agents bid once; a farm pays a fresh auction price per puppet per round.
